text:
sara: Heads up — after the 03:00 deploy we saw sustained NVMe IOPS spikes in us-west1 that blocked GPU attaches for ~7m. Ephemeral cleaner started at 03:02 and overlapped a batch ramp. Ops noticed queue depth hitting 512.

matt: Which hosts? any quick sysstat/iostat snapshot?

sara: gnode-744, gnode-745, gnode-746. Pasted iostat -x from gnode-744 at 03:05: 
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await svctm  %util
nvme0n1        980.00  120.00  7900.0  1200.0  24.50  2.10  95.60
```

liam: ugh, %util ~95 — cleaner + batch writes is killing it. Did the cleaner run across the pool in parallel?

sara: yes, the janitor cron launched cleaners on the whole shard at the same time (we mis-scheduled the monthly deep-scrub during the nightly batch window).

hina: Any sign of corruption or SMART errors? we saw a couple of CRC errors last month on similar hosts.

sara: No new SMARTs, just high latencies. checksum scans completed but slow. Noted increased retry counts in kernel logs.

matt: Short term mitigation: pause janitor on the three nodes and postpone the deep-scrub for this window. I'll push a kill + reschedule. Also increasing IO weight for batch to reduce random writes might help.

liam: Medium term: add a safety throttle in janitor: if device util > 80% or iops > 800 for 30s, back off and sleep random(30-120s).

hina: We should also consider wear tradeoffs — pausing scrub defers cleanup but avoids transient provisioning failures. Capture how long scrubs were queued so we can estimate backlog growth.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1345 — "us-west1 ephemeral NVMe IOPS spike causing GPU attach failures". Link: https://incidents/redwood/INC-2026-1345 

sara: Action items: @matt pause janitor on impacted hosts (done), @liam add throttle hook to janitor, @hina add alert for sustained nvme %util > 85 for 2m. I'll follow up with a postmortem doc and recommend moving deep-scrub out of nightly batch window. :thumbsup:

matt: paused janitor on gnode-744/745/746, observed attach success rate recovered. Will open PR for backpressure today.

liam: PR for janitor backpressure draft: https://git/redwood/janitor/pull/548 (adds util/iops check + exponential backoff).

hina: I'll create the alert in PagerDuty and add a runbook blurb about rescheduling deep scrubs to <non-batch> windows.

sara: Thanks — keeping this thread for follow-up. Postmortem will include timeline, cost impact (GPU minutes lost), and scrub scheduling policy change.
